chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdullah (peace be upon him)

He said: Asking permission (to enter) is done three times: the first time so they hear, the second time so they prepare (cover up), and the third time if they wish they grant permission, and if they wish they do not, so the one asking permission returns.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper Islamic etiquette for asking permission to enter a room?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the prophetic etiquette of *al-istidhan* (seeking permission), emphasizing that it is not merely a physical act but a spiritual discipline of humility and respect for privacy. The three stages—ensuring hearing, allowing preparation, and granting discretionary choice—reflect the Quranic principle of avoiding intrusion into private spheres, reinforcing the social ethics of the Ahl al-Bayt. This practice is often cited by Shia jurists to derive the ruling that entering without proper permission is a violation of the occupant's right to privacy.
